subject: File download issues with Shiny Server behind an Apache Reverse Proxy

messages.author: f12d0a72c2381adf
messages.subject: File download issues with Shiny Server behind an Apache Reverse Proxy
parts:
Hi all,

we're running the Open Source edition of Shiny Server behind an Apache Reverse Proxy and we cannot seem to get file downloads (using Shiny's downloadHandler() function) working.

This is our Apache configuration:

<Location /dashboard>
  ProxyPass http://localhost:3838/dashboard
  ProxyPassReverse  http://localhost:3838/dashboard
</Location>

The Shiny app "dashboard" is running smoothly, no problems here, but whenever we try downloading a file, all we get is a text file containing the temp file name of the download. The file gets correctly created in /tmp/RtmpSA9lN2/file2de0487d470a (or whatever :-) ), but instead of serving up this file, Apache serves a file containing only this filename as text content.

Here's a curl output of what happens:

$ curl -v 'https://[removed]/dashboard/session/[removed]/download/downloadReport?w='
[SSL stuff removed]
> GET /dashboard/session/[removed]/download/downloadReport?w= HTTP/1.1
> User-Agent: curl/7.24.0 (x86_64-apple-darwin12.0) libcurl/7.24.0 OpenSSL/0.9.8y zlib/1.2.5
> Host: [removed]
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Date: Mon, 28 Oct 2013 14:09:31 GMT
< content-disposition: attachment; filename="My_Report.html"
< cache-control: no-cache
< x-ua-compatible: chrome=1
< content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
< content-length: 32
<
* Connection #0 to host [removed] left intact
/tmp/RtmpSA9lN2/file2de0487d470a* Closing connection #0

This is the code used in server.R for specifying the downloadHandler:

  output$downloadReport <- downloadHandler('lc_report.html',
                                           content = function(file) {
                                             file.copy('report/lc_report.html',
                                                       file)
                                           },
                                           'text/html')
                                          
Downloads work perfectly fine when the app is executed locally via runApp().

Has anyone encountered a solution/workaround for this issue?

Thanks!

Alex
